questions.stem: Why is selective reabsorption described as 'selective'?

options.text: Because the process only occurs when the body selects it to happen
Because it selects which waste products to excrete first
Because it only happens in selected nephrons
Because only certain useful substances are reabsorbed, not waste products

questions.explanation: The process is called 'selective' because only useful substances like glucose, amino acids, and water are reabsorbed back into the blood. Waste products like urea are left in the filtrate to be excreted.
